input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: The first Section 2.2 imposes a full-term sole-and-exclusive-supplier obligation on Customer for hosted analytics services, with no category limit, no 12-month cap, and no automatic exit for service-level or delivery-date failures — walk-away territory under the rule, well short of the fallback. Section 12.3's statement that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment is countervailing but directly contradicted by Section 2.2, so the contradictory operative grant must be fixed rather than relied upon. We therefore made the appointment non-exclusive, achieving the preferred position with the shortest edit and aligning Section 2.2 with Section 12.3.

ops.oldText: Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term
ops.newText: a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services; Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot commit to Copperleaf as sole and exclusive provider, and that commitment contradicts Section 12.3, under which we make no exclusivity commitment; we have made the appointment non-exclusive. If exclusivity matters commercially, we could discuss a defined category capped at 12 months that ends automatically on any service-level or delivery-date failure.
proposal.summary: Convert the sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment into a non-exclusive appointment with no sole-supplier obligation.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
